words.gloss: on the measure of eating (chapter name)

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम मात्राशितीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter Mātrāśitīya (On the Measure of Eating).
notes: Prose opening formula (typed as 'verse'). mātrāśitīya is a taddhita name from the chapter's opening words mātrāśī syāt.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula. sma with āha gives a past sense.

hindi: मात्राशी होना चाहिए।
english: One should be an eater in measure (mātrāśī).
notes: Prose sūtra (typed as 'verse'). The Hindi keeps the term मात्राशी; the subject (one, a person) is implied by the optative.

words.gloss: dependent on the strength of the digestive fire

hindi: और आहार की मात्रा अग्नि के बल की अपेक्षा रखती है।
english: And the measure of food depends on the strength of the digestive fire (agni).
notes: punar here connects ('and', 'moreover'), not 'again'.

hindi: क्योंकि इसका खाया हुआ जितना भोजन प्रकृति को हानि पहुँचाए बिना यथासमय पच जाता है, उतना इसकी मात्रा का प्रमाण जानना चाहिए।
english: For as much food eaten by him as, without harming his natural state (prakṛti), goes to digestion in due time, so much is to be known as the measure of his quantity.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). jarā here is digestion (jaraṇa), not old age. mātrāpramāṇa: 'the measure (pramāṇa) of the quantity (mātrā)'; it can also be read as one idea, 'the right measure'.
lines_deva: यावद्ध्यस्याशनमशितमनुपहत्य प्रकृतिं यथाकालं जरां गच्छति तावदस्य मात्राप्रमाणं वेदितव्यं भवति
lines_iast: yāvaddhyasyāśanamaśitamanupahatya prakṛtiṃ yathākālaṃ jarāṃ gacchati tāvadasya mātrāpramāṇaṃ veditavyaṃ bhavati

words.gloss: śāli rice, ṣaṣṭika rice, mudga, lāva, kapiñjala, eṇa, hare, śarabha, śambara and the like

hindi: इनमें शालि, षष्टिक, मुद्ग, लाव, कपिञ्जल, एण, शश, शरभ, शम्बर आदि आहार-द्रव्य प्रकृति से लघु होने पर भी मात्रा की अपेक्षा रखते हैं।
english: In this matter, food substances such as śāli rice, ṣaṣṭika rice, mudga, lāva, kapiñjala, eṇa, hare (śaśa), śarabha and śambara, although light by nature, depend on measure.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). Identifications: śāli = a winter rice, ṣaṣṭika = a sixty-day rice (Oryza sativa varieties, standard); mudga = green gram, Vigna radiata (standard); lāva = a quail (probable); kapiñjala = grey partridge (probable); eṇa = a black antelope (probable); śarabha = a large deer or wild goat (disputed); śambara = sambar deer (probable).

words.gloss: flour, sugar-cane, products of milk, tila, māṣa, meat of marsh and water animals and the like

hindi: इसी प्रकार पिष्ट, इक्षु, क्षीर-विकृति, तिल, माष, आनूप और औदक मांस आदि आहार-द्रव्य प्रकृति से गुरु होने पर भी मात्रा की ही अपेक्षा रखते हैं।
english: Likewise food substances such as flour (preparations), sugar-cane, products of milk, tila, māṣa, and the meat of marsh (ānūpa) and water (audaka) animals, although heavy by nature, depend on measure itself.

text_flags.why: One syllable 'ti' seems lost (haplography): 'vikṛti-lamāṣa' gives no word, while vikṛti + tila + māṣa fits the list of heavy foods; the Devanagari has the same gap (विकृतिलमाषा). Possible typing error.

notes: eva with mātrām: 'depend on measure itself' (as much as the light ones do). kṣīravikṛti = milk products (curd etc.). ānūpa = of marshy land; audaka = of water animals; piśita = meat, taken with both. Identifications: tila = sesame, Sesamum indicum (standard); māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard); ikṣu = sugar-cane, Saccharum officinarum (standard).

words.gram: n. loc. sg. (or n. nom./acc. du.)

words.gloss: abounding in qualities of air and fire
abounding in qualities of earth and soma
by nature kindlers of the fire
by nature kindlers of the fire
strength from exercise and of the fire
dependent on the strength of the fire

hindi: ऐसा कहे जाने पर द्रव्य में गुरुता और लघुता को अकारण न माने; क्योंकि लघु द्रव्य वायु और अग्नि के गुणों की बहुलता वाले होते हैं, और अन्य द्रव्य पृथ्वी और सोम के गुणों की बहुलता वाले। इसलिए लघु द्रव्य अपने गुण से भी अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने के स्वभाव वाले होते हैं, और सौहित्य तक सेवन किए जाने पर भी अल्प दोष वाले कहे जाते हैं; किन्तु गुरु द्रव्य असमानता के कारण अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने के स्वभाव वाले नहीं होते, और इसलिए सौहित्य तक सेवन किए जाने पर अत्यधिक दोषयुक्त होते हैं, व्यायाम और अग्नि के बल के सिवा। यही वह मात्रा है जो अग्नि के बल की अपेक्षा रखती है।
english: And when this has been said, one should not think that heaviness and lightness in a substance are of no account; for light substances abound in the qualities of air (vāyu) and fire (agni), and the others abound in the qualities of earth and soma. Therefore light substances, even by their own quality, are by nature kindlers of the fire, and are said to be of little harm even when taken to satiety; heavy substances, however, are not by nature kindlers of the fire, because of dissimilarity, and hence, taken to satiety, they are excessively harmful, except where there is strength from exercise and strength of the fire. This is the measure that depends on the strength of the fire.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). 'the others' (itarāṇi) are the heavy substances. vāyu here is the element air (beside fire, earth and soma), so it is rendered 'air', not Vāta. soma is the watery, cooling principle (here paired with earth). asāmānyāt: because they are unlike (not of the same nature as) fire. vyāyāmāgnibalāt can be read 'strength (gained) by exercise and strength of fire' or 'strength of fire from exercise'. dravye in 'na caivamukte dravye' is taken as loc. sg. ('in a substance'); it may also go with ukte as a locative absolute, 'when (the measure) has been said (to depend on fire) with regard to substance'.
lines_deva: न चैवमुक्ते द्रव्ये गुरुलाघवमकारणं मन्येत, लघूनि हि द्रव्याणि वाय्वग्निगुणबहुलानि भवन्ति; पृथ्वीसोमगुणबहुलानीतराणि, तस्मात् स्वगुणादपि लघून्यग्निसन्धुक्षणस्वभावान्यल्पदोषाणि चोच्यन्तेऽपि सौहित्योपयुक्तानि, गुरूणि पुनर्नाग्निसन्धुक्षणस्वभावान्यसामान्यात्, अतश्चातिमात्रं दोषवन्ति सौहित्योपयुक्तान्यन्यत्र व्यायामाग्निबलात्; सैषा भवत्यग्निबलापेक्षिणी मात्रा
lines_iast: na caivamukte dravye gurulāghavamakāraṇaṃ manyeta, laghūni hi dravyāṇi vāyvagniguṇabahulāni bhavanti; pṛthvīsomaguṇabahulānītarāṇi, tasmāt svaguṇādapi laghūnyagnisandhukṣaṇasvabhāvānyalpadoṣāṇi cocyante'pi sauhityopayuktāni, gurūṇi punarnāgnisandhukṣaṇasvabhāvānyasāmānyāt, ataścātimātraṃ doṣavanti sauhityopayuktānyanyatra vyāyāmāgnibalāt; saiṣā bhavatyagnibalāpekṣiṇī mātrā

hindi: और यह बात नहीं कि मात्रा द्रव्य की अपेक्षा नहीं रखती; द्रव्य की अपेक्षा से गुरु द्रव्यों का त्रिभाग-सौहित्य या अर्ध-सौहित्य उपदिष्ट है, और लघु द्रव्यों का भी अति-सौहित्य नहीं, अग्नि की युक्ति के लिए।
english: And it is not that (the measure) does not depend on the substance: with regard to the substance, a third part of satiety or half satiety is prescribed for heavy substances, and for light ones too not excessive satiety, for the sake of the right ordering (yukti) of the fire.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). Subject of nāpekṣate is understood as mātrā from unit 6. tribhāgasauhitya is read by commentators as filling to a third of one's capacity (or eating up to two-thirds); the literal sense is 'satiety by a third part'. agner yuktyartham: 'for keeping the fire in proper order'; yukti may also mean 'proper application'.
lines_deva: न च नापेक्षते द्रव्यं; द्रव्यापेक्षया च त्रिभागसौहित्यमर्धसौहित्यं वा गुरूणामुपदिश्यते, लघूनामपि च नातिसौहित्यमग्नेर्युक्त्यर्थम्
lines_iast: na ca nāpekṣate dravyaṃ; dravyāpekṣayā ca tribhāgasauhityamardhasauhityaṃ vā gurūṇāmupadiśyate, laghūnāmapi ca nātisauhityamagneryuktyartham

words.gloss: with strength, complexion, happiness and life

hindi: क्योंकि मात्रा के अनुसार खाया गया भोजन प्रकृति को हानि पहुँचाए बिना खाने वाले को अवश्य बल, वर्ण, सुख और आयु से युक्त करता है।
english: For food eaten in measure, without harming the natural state (prakṛti), certainly endows the one who takes it with strength, complexion, happiness and life.
notes: Prose (typed as 'verse'). iti closes the prose section before the verses.

hindi: और यहाँ श्लोक हैं — इसलिए भोजन कर चुका मनुष्य गुरु पिष्टमय पदार्थ, तण्डुल और पृथुक भी कभी न खाए; भूखा होने पर मात्रा से खाए।
english: And here there are (verses): therefore one who has eaten should never eat what is heavy and made of flour, nor rice grains (taṇḍula) and flattened rice (pṛthuka); when hungry, one should eat in measure.
notes: Line 1 is the lead-in formula 'bhavanti cātra' (and here there are verses), with a printed dash. guru piṣṭamayam can be read as one object ('heavy flour-food') or 'flour-food, which is heavy'. taṇḍula here is commonly taken as parched or prepared rice grains; the text says only 'rice grains'. mātrām: 'in measure', adverbial accusative.

hindi: वल्लूर, सूखे शाक, शालूक और बिस का गुरु होने के कारण अभ्यास न करे; कृश मांस का तो उपयोग ही न करे।
english: Dried meat (vallūra), dried vegetables, lotus rhizomes (śālūka) and lotus stalks (bisa) one should not use habitually, because of their heaviness; lean meat one should not use at all.
notes: māṃsaṃ kṛśam: literally 'lean (emaciated) meat'; commentators take it as meat of an emaciated animal. gauravāt may also be read with māṃsam only. śālūka and bisa are parts of the lotus (Nelumbo nucifera, standard).

hindi: मत्स्य, दधि, माष और यवक का अभ्यास न करे।
english: Fish, curd, māṣa and yavaka one should not use habitually.
notes: GROUPING: the unit has only one half-verse. Other editions are recalled as having a first half before it (listing kūrcikā, kilāṭa, pork, beef and buffalo meat); this was not checked against a second source here, so it is a possible omission in the typed text, not applied. Identifications: māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard); yavaka = an inferior kind of barley (probable).
lines_deva: मत्स्यान् दधि च माषांश्च यवकांश्च न शीलयेत्
lines_iast: matsyān dadhi ca māṣāṃśca yavakāṃśca na śīlayet

hindi: षष्टिक, शालि और मुद्ग, सैन्धव और आमलक, यव, आन्तरिक्ष जल, सर्पि, जांगल और मधु का अभ्यास करे।
english: Ṣaṣṭika rice, śāli rice and mudga, rock salt (saindhava) and āmalaka, barley (yava), water from the sky, ghee, jāṅgala (meat of dry-land animals) and honey one should use habitually.

text_flags.why: piṣṭika gives no fitting sense in a list of wholesome foods; ṣaṣṭika rice with śāli and mudga is the pair already named in unit 5 (śāliṣaṣṭikamudga...). The Devanagari has the same form (पिष्टिका). Possible typing error.

notes: jāṅgala alone stands for jāṅgala meat (meat of animals of dry land); payaḥ here is water (āntarīkṣa, rain-water), not milk. Identification: āmalaka = Indian gooseberry, Phyllanthus emblica (standard).

hindi: और उसका नित्य प्रयोग करे जिससे स्वास्थ्य बना रहता है और जो अजात विकारों की अनुत्पत्ति करने वाला है।
english: And one should always use that by which health continues, and which causes disorders not yet arisen not to arise.

words.gloss: beginning with collyrium for the eyes

hindi: इसके बाद स्वस्थवृत्त को ध्यान में रखकर शरीर के लिए करणीय अक्षि-अञ्जन आदि कर्म गुणों सहित कहा जाएगा।
english: After this, the bodily practice beginning with collyrium for the eyes will be declared together with its benefits, with a view to the regimen of the healthy (svasthavṛtti).
notes: saṃpravakṣyate: middle future with passive sense ('will be declared'). guṇataḥ: 'according to (its) benefits'.

hindi: नेत्रों के लिए हितकर सौवीर अञ्जन का नित्य प्रयोग करे, और पाँच या आठ रात्रि में स्रावण के लिए रसाञ्जन का।
english: One should daily apply sauvīra collyrium, beneficial to the eyes, and rasāñjana in five or eight nights for the purpose of drawing out secretion.
notes: pañcarātre 'ṣṭarātre: 'at five or eight nights', commonly taken as 'once every five or eight nights'. srāvaṇārthe: for making the eyes run (discharge). Identifications: sauvīrāñjana = a black antimony or lead ore collyrium (disputed); rasāñjana = an extract of Berberis aristata (dāruharidrā) (standard).

hindi: चक्षु तेजोमय है, उसे विशेष रूप से श्लेष्मा से भय है; इसलिए श्लेष्मा को हरने वाला कर्म हितकर है, जो दृष्टि का प्रसादन करता है।
english: The eye is made of fire (tejas); for it there is danger especially from Kapha (śleṣman); therefore a procedure that removes Kapha is beneficial, clearing the sight.
notes: hitaṃ dṛṣṭeḥ prasādanam: 'beneficial (and) clearing of the sight'; dṛṣṭeḥ may also go with hitam ('beneficial to the sight').
lines_deva: ततः श्लेष्महरं कर्म हितं दृष्टेः प्रसादनम्
lines_iast: tataḥ śleṣmaharaṃ karma hitaṃ dṛṣṭeḥ prasādanam

hindi: वह तीक्ष्ण अञ्जन दिन में नेत्रों में प्रयोग नहीं करना चाहिए; विरेक से दुर्बल हुई दृष्टि सूर्य को प्राप्त कर क्षीण हो जाती है।
english: That sharp collyrium should not be applied to the eyes by day: the sight, weakened by the evacuation (vireka), is impaired on meeting the sun.
notes: tat refers to the draining collyrium (rasāñjana) of unit 15. vireka here is the drawing out of secretion from the eye. sīdati literally 'sinks'.

words.gram: n. gen. pl. (metrically short for malinānām)

hindi: इसलिए स्राव्य अञ्जन तो रात में निश्चित रूप से अभीष्ट है। क्योंकि जैसे विविध प्रकार के मलिन कनक आदि का
english: Therefore the draining collyrium is certainly recommended at night. For just as of gold and the like, of various kinds, when soiled,
notes: GROUPING: the edition's numbering runs half a verse behind the sense from here on: line b (yathā hi ...) begins a simile that continues through unit 19 and ends at 20a (... nabhasīnduvat); 20b begins the drug list of the head-evacuating wick, which runs to 23a. Kept as printed. malināṃ is taken as gen. pl. 'soiled' agreeing with kanakādīnām; the regular form is malinānām (one syllable more, which would break the 8-syllable pāda), so the printed short form is likely metrical or an old reading; not flagged as a typo.

words.gloss: by oil, cloth, hair-brush and the like
by collyrium, eye-drops and the like

hindi: धोए जाने पर तैल, चेल, कच आदि से निर्मल शुद्धि होती है, वैसे ही मनुष्यों के नेत्रों में अञ्जन, आश्च्योतन आदि से
english: when washed with oil, cloth, hair and the like, there is a stainless cleanness, so in the eyes of mortals, by collyrium, eye-drops (āścyotana) and the like,
notes: GROUPING: continues the simile of 18b and runs on to 20a. kaca: 'hair', commonly taken as a brush of hair used for polishing metal.

hindi: दृष्टि निर्मल आकाश में चन्द्रमा की भाँति निराकुल चमकती है। हरेणुका, प्रियङ्गु, पृथ्वीका, केशर, नख,
english: the sight shines undisturbed, like the moon in a clear sky. Hareṇukā, priyaṅgu, pṛthvīkā, keśara, nakha,
notes: GROUPING: 20a ends the simile of 18b-19; 20b begins the list of drugs for the wick (governed by piṣṭvā limpet in 23b). Identifications: hareṇukā = Vitex agnus-castus seed (disputed); priyaṅgu = Callicarpa macrophylla (probable); pṛthvīkā = large cardamom or nigella (disputed); keśara = nāgakeśara, Mesua ferrea (probable); nakha = a fragrant operculum of a shell (probable).
lines_deva: हरेणुकां प्रियङ्गुं च पृथ्वीकां केशरं नखम्
lines_iast: hareṇukāṃ priyaṅguṃ ca pṛthvīkāṃ keśaraṃ nakham

hindi: ह्रीवेर, चन्दन, पत्र, त्वक्, एला, उशीर, पद्मक, ध्यामक, मधुक, मांसी, गुग्गुलु, अगुरु, शर्करा,
english: hrīvera, candana, patra, tvak, elā, uśīra, padmaka, dhyāmaka, madhuka, māṃsī, guggulu, aguru, śarkarā,
notes: GROUPING: part of the drug list running from 20b to 23a. māṃsī stands in the nominative inside an accusative list (a loose construction, or a pausal form); sense unaffected. śarkara here is taken as śarkarā (sugar), made neuter as the last member of the samāhāra dvandva. Identifications: hrīvera = Pavonia odorata (probable); candana = sandalwood, Santalum album (standard); patra = tejapatra, Cinnamomum tamala (standard); tvak = cinnamon bark (standard); elā = cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum (standard); uśīra = vetiver, Chrysopogon zizanioides (standard); padmaka = Prunus cerasoides (standard); dhyāmaka = a fragrant grass, Cymbopogon species (probable); madhuka = liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra (standard); māṃsī = jaṭāmāṃsī, Nardostachys jatamansi (standard); guggulu = Commiphora wightii resin (standard); aguru = agarwood, Aquilaria agallocha (standard).

words.gloss: barks of nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa and lodhra
words.gram: f. acc. pl. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: न्यग्रोध, उदुम्बर, अश्वत्थ, प्लक्ष और लोध्र की उत्तम छालें, वन्य, सर्जरस, मुस्त, शैलेय, कमल और उत्पल,
english: good barks of nyagrodha, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa and lodhra; vanya, sarjarasa, musta, śaileya, kamala and utpala,
notes: GROUPING: part of the drug list 20b-23a. Identifications: nyagrodha = Ficus benghalensis (standard); udumbara = Ficus racemosa (standard); aśvattha = Ficus religiosa (standard); plakṣa = Ficus lacor or Ficus virens (disputed); lodhra = Symplocos racemosa (standard); vanya = kaivarta-mustaka, a sedge (disputed); sarjarasa = resin of Vateria indica or Shorea robusta (disputed); musta = Cyperus rotundus (standard); śaileya = a lichen, Parmelia species (probable); kamala = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera (standard); utpala = water-lily, Nymphaea species (standard).

hindi: श्रीवेष्टक, शल्लकी और शुकबर्ह भी — इन्हें पीसकर शरेषीका पर लेप करे; उस यव-सदृश वर्ति को
english: śrīveṣṭaka, śallakī and also śukabarha: having ground (these), one should smear (them) on a reed-stalk (śareṣīkā); that wick, resembling a barley grain,

text_flags.why: ṣarha gives no word; śukabarha (a fragrant drug, 'parrot-feather') is the expected member of the list, and ṣ for b is a common slip. The Devanagari has the same form (शुकषर्ह). Possible typing error.

notes: GROUPING: 23a ends the drug list begun at 20b; 23b begins the making of the wick, which continues to 25a (... pibet prāyogikīṃ sukhām). Identifications: śrīveṣṭaka = turpentine resin of Pinus roxburghii (probable); śallakī = Boswellia serrata (standard); śukabarha = sthauṇeyaka, Taxus or Clerodendrum species (disputed). yavasannibhā: shaped like a barley grain, i.e. thick in the middle and tapering.

hindi: चिकित्सक उसे अङ्गुष्ठ-संमित और आठ अङ्गुल के बराबर बनाए। उस सूखी, निगर्भ वर्ति को धूमनेत्र में लगाकर मनुष्य
english: the physician should make (it) of a thumb's measure and equal to eight finger-breadths. That wick, dried, with its core removed, fitted into a smoking-pipe (dhūmanetra), a man
notes: GROUPING: continues the wick of 23b and runs on to 25a. aṅguṣṭhasaṃmitā is taken as 'as thick as the thumb' and aṣṭāṅgulasamā as 'eight aṅgula long' (the text names the two measures without 'thick'/'long'). nigarbhā: commentators explain it as with the reed (śareṣīkā) pulled out once the paste is dry; the regular form would be nirgarbhā.
lines_deva: शुष्कां निगर्भां तां वर्तिं धूमनेत्रार्पितां नरः
lines_iast: śuṣkāṃ nigarbhāṃ tāṃ vartiṃ dhūmanetrārpitāṃ naraḥ

hindi: स्नेह से लिप्त, अग्नि से जलाई हुई, सुखद प्रायोगिकी को पिए। वसा, घृत और मधूच्छिष्ट से, युक्ति से युक्त उत्तम औषधों से,
english: smeared with fat (sneha) and lit by fire, should drink (it): the pleasant prāyogikī (regular smoke). With muscle-fat (vasā), ghee and beeswax (madhūcchiṣṭa), with excellent medicines joined with rational planning (yukti),
notes: GROUPING: 25a ends the prāyogika (regular) smoking begun at 23b; 25b begins the snaihika (unctuous) smoking, completed at 26a. vasāghṛtamadhūcchiṣṭaiḥ may also be read as a separate instrumental beside varauṣadhaiḥ; together they govern kṛtvā in 26a. madhūcchiṣṭa = beeswax (standard). prāyogikī (feminine, agreeing with varti) is the name of the regular, daily kind of smoking.

hindi: मधुरकों से स्नैहिकी वर्ति बनाकर धूम का सेवन करे। श्वेता, ज्योतिष्मती, हरिताल और मनःशिला,
english: having made the unctuous (snaihikī) wick with the madhuraka (sweet) drugs, one should practise smoking. Śvetā and jyotiṣmatī, haritāla, manaḥśilā,
notes: GROUPING: 26a ends the snaihika smoking of 25b; 26b begins the list for head-evacuating smoke (mūrdhavirecana), completed at 27a. dhūmam is masculine while snaihikīm is feminine: snaihikīm agrees with an understood varti or is used loosely; sense is 'unctuous smoking'. madhuraka = the sweet group of drugs (jīvanīya etc.). Identifications: śvetā = white aparājitā, Clitoria ternatea (probable); jyotiṣmatī = Celastrus paniculatus (standard); haritāla = orpiment, arsenic trisulphide (standard); manaḥśilā = realgar, arsenic disulphide (standard). Correction (review): snaihikīm agrees with vartim ('the unctuous wick'), as prāyogikīm does in 25a; the remark that it goes loosely with dhūmam is withdrawn.

hindi: और अगुरु, पत्र आदि गन्ध — मूर्धविरेचन में धूम। सिर का गौरव, शूल, पीनस और अर्धावभेदक,
english: and fragrant substances such as aguru and patra: the smoke in head-evacuation (mūrdhavirecana). Heaviness of the head, pain, pīnasa and ardhāvabhedaka,
notes: GROUPING: 27a ends the head-evacuating smoke list begun at 26b; 27b begins the list of disorders relieved by smoking, which runs to 31a (... dhūmapānāt praśāmyanti). The construction of 27a is elliptical (no verb); dhūmam is taken as 'the smoke (consisting of these)'. śirasaḥ may go with both gauravam and śūlam. Modern equivalents: pīnasa = chronic rhinitis or coryza (probable); ardhāvabhedaka = hemicrania, migraine-like one-sided headache (probable).

words.gloss: arising from disorder of ear, nose and eye

hindi: कर्ण और अक्षि का शूल, कास, हिक्का और श्वास, गलग्रह, दन्तों की दुर्बलता, श्रोत्र, घ्राण और अक्षि के दोष से उत्पन्न आस्राव,
english: pain of ear and eye, cough (kāsa), hiccup and dyspnoea (śvāsa), seizure of the throat (galagraha), weakness of the teeth, discharge arising from disorder of ear, nose and eye,
notes: GROUPING: part of the list of disorders 27b-31a. galagraha: literally 'seizure of the throat' (stiffness or obstruction). doṣa in śrotraghrāṇākṣidoṣaja may mean 'disorder' or 'the doṣa (of those organs)'.

hindi: घ्राण और आस्य की पूति-गन्ध, दन्तशूल, अरोचक, हनु और मन्या का ग्रह, कण्डू, कृमि, मुख में पाण्डुता,
english: foul smell of nose and mouth, toothache, loss of taste (arocaka), stiffness of the jaw and the neck (manyā), itching, worms (krimi), pallor in the face,
notes: GROUPING: part of the list of disorders 27b-31a. mukhe may go with kaṇḍūḥ, krimayaḥ and pāṇḍutā together ('itching, worms and pallor in the mouth/face'); mukha may mean mouth or face. pūti is taken as an adjective 'foul' with gandha; it may also be a separate noun 'putrefaction'.

hindi: श्लेष्मा का प्रसेक, वैस्वर्य, गलशुण्डी, उपजिह्विका, खालित्य, केशों का पिञ्जरत्व और पतन भी,
english: flow of Kapha (śleṣman), hoarseness, galaśuṇḍī and upajihvikā, baldness, tawniness and also falling of the hair,
notes: GROUPING: part of the list of disorders 27b-31a. galaśuṇḍyupajihvikā may be read as two items in a dvandva (galaśuṇḍī + upajihvikā, nom. sg. of the last). Modern equivalents: galaśuṇḍī = enlarged uvula or tonsillitis (probable); upajihvikā = swelling under the tongue, ranula (probable); khālitya = alopecia (standard); piñjaratva = greying or reddish-tawny hair (probable).
lines_deva: खालित्यं पिञ्जरत्वं च केशानां पतनं तथा
lines_iast: khālityaṃ piñjaratvaṃ ca keśānāṃ patanaṃ tathā

hindi: क्षवथु, अतितन्द्रा, बुद्धि का मोह और अतिनिद्रा धूमपान से शान्त होते हैं; और बल अधिक होता है
english: sneezing, excessive drowsiness, confusion of the intellect and excessive sleep are allayed by smoking (dhūmapāna); and strength becomes greater
notes: GROUPING: 31a ends the list of disorders begun at 27b; 31b begins a new sentence completed at 32a (balaṃ ... śiroruhakapālānām ...). kṣavathu: here taken as excessive sneezing.

words.gloss: of the hair and the skull
having Vāta and Kapha as their nature

hindi: शिरोरुह, कपाल, इन्द्रियों और स्वर का। और वात-कफ-स्वरूप, ऊर्ध्वजत्रु में उत्पन्न, बलवान् भी
english: of the hair, the skull, the sense organs and the voice. And of the nature of Vāta and Kapha, arising above the collar-bones (ūrdhvajatru), even strong
notes: GROUPING: 32a ends the sentence of 31b; 32b begins a sentence completed at 33a (... vyādhayaḥ syuḥ śirogatāḥ). śiroruha (hair, literally 'what grows on the head'). kapāla may mean skull or forehead.

words.gloss: of one who drinks smoke by the mouth (meaning uncertain)
in the drinking for regular use

hindi: धूम को वक्त्र से पीने वाले के शिरोगत व्याधियाँ नहीं होतीं। उसके प्रयोग-पान में आठ काल कहे गए हैं।
english: diseases located in the head would not occur to one who drinks smoke by the mouth. For its drinking in regular use, eight times are declared.
notes: GROUPING: 33a completes the sentence begun at 32b (na ca ... vyādhayaḥ syuḥ: 'would not occur'); 33b begins the eight times, explained at 34-35a. dhūmavaktrakapānasya is obscure: it is taken here as dhūma + vaktraka (mouth; -ka without change of sense) + pāna, 'of one whose drinking of smoke is by the mouth', i.e. one who smokes; other analyses (with ka = head, or a different reading) are possible. The negation 'not' in both translations comes from 'na ca' in 32b. tasya refers to dhūma (smoke). prayogapāna = the drinking of the prāyogika (regular) smoke.

words.gloss: stirring up of Vāta and Kapha

hindi: क्योंकि इन कालों में वात और श्लेष्मा का समुत्क्लेश देखा जाता है। स्नान करके, भोजन करके, समुल्लेखन करके, छींककर और दन्तों को घिसकर,
english: For at these times a stirring up of Vāta and Kapha (śleṣman) is seen. After bathing, after eating, after scraping, after sneezing, and after rubbing the teeth,
notes: GROUPING: 34a explains the eight times of 33b; 34b begins the list of the times, completed at 35a (... dhūmapo bhavet). samullikhya: 'having scraped'; commentators take it as scraping the tongue (or, by some, vomiting); the text gives no object.
lines_deva: स्नात्वा भुक्त्वा समुल्लिख्य क्षुत्वा दन्तान्निघृष्य च
lines_iast: snātvā bhuktvā samullikhya kṣutvā dantānnighṛṣya ca

words.gloss: at the end of nasal therapy, collyrium and sleep
words.gram: m. loc. sg. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: having Vāta and Kapha as their nature

hindi: और नावन, अञ्जन और निद्रा के अन्त में आत्मवान् धूमप बने। इस प्रकार वात-कफ-स्वरूप, ऊर्ध्वजत्रुज नहीं होते
english: and at the end of nasal therapy (nāvana), collyrium and sleep, the self-controlled man should be a smoke-drinker. Thus, of the nature of Vāta and Kapha and arising above the collar-bones, do not occur
notes: GROUPING: 35a ends the list of eight times begun at 34b (bathing, eating, scraping, sneezing, rubbing the teeth, after nāvana, after añjana, after sleep); 35b begins a sentence whose subject rogāḥ comes in 36a. nāvana = nasal therapy (nasya).

hindi: रोग उसको। किन्तु पेय आपान तीन बार तीन-तीन हों। बुद्धिमान् अधिक से अधिक दिन के कालों में दो-काल-पायी हो।
english: diseases to him. But the bouts (āpāna) to be drunk should be three times three each. At most, the wise man should drink (smoke) at two of the times in a day.
notes: GROUPING: 36a 'rogās tasya' completes the sentence of 35b (diseases ... do not occur to him); the rest of 36a begins the rule of draughts. triḥ trayas trayaḥ is commonly taken as 'three bouts of three puffs each'; the literal words are 'thrice, three, three'. paraṃ may mean 'at most' or 'beyond (that)'; ahnaḥ kāleṣu: 'at (the eight) times in the day'. The negation for 'rogās tasya' comes from 'na bhavanti' in 35b.

words.gloss: cleansing of heart, throat and senses

hindi: प्रायोगिक धूमपान में। किन्तु स्नैहिक में एक बार, और वैरेचनिक धूम को तीन या चार बार पिए। हृदय, कण्ठ और इन्द्रियों की शुद्धि, सिर का हल्कापन, शमन —
english: in regular (prāyogika) smoking. But in the unctuous (snaihika) one should drink once, and the evacuative (vairecana) smoke three or four times. Cleansing of the heart, throat and senses, lightness of the head, calming —

text_flags.why: possible: a locative 'vairecye' (in the evacuative smoking) would be parallel to 'prayoge' and 'snaihike'; the accusative as printed is also grammatical ('the evacuative smoke one should drink'), so the printed form is kept in the split.

notes: GROUPING: in this edition the numbered units in this chunk run a half-verse out of step with the sentences: each sentence (and, it seems, each verse of the usual numbering) runs from line 2 of one unit to line 1 of the next (here line 1 completes 36b, and line 2 begins the sentence that ends in 38a). Kept as given. 'prayoge' = the regular (prāyogika) smoking named 'prayogapāna' in unit 33. The commas are printed in the source and kept in the tokens. 'śamaḥ' governs 'yatheritānāṃ doṣāṇām' in the next unit (calming of the doṣas). Review: 'prayoge,' (with the printed comma) completes 36b: in regular smoking one drinks at most at two times of the day; 'tu' then contrasts snaihika (once) and vairecana (three or four times).
lines_deva: प्रयोगे, स्नैहिके त्वेकं, वैरेच्यं त्रिचतुः पिबेत्
lines_iast: prayoge, snaihike tvekaṃ, vairecyaṃ tricatuḥ pibet

hindi: यथा-ईरित दोषों का — यह सम्यक् पिए जाने का लक्षण है। बधिरता, अन्धता और मूकता, रक्तपित्त, सिर का भ्रम —
english: of the doṣas as stirred up — is the sign of proper drinking. Deafness, blindness and dumbness, raktapitta, giddiness of the head —
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 1 ends the sentence begun in 37b, line 2 begins the list that is the object of 'kuryād upadravān' in 39a. 'yatheritānām': īrita from √īr 'set in motion, stirred'; it can also mean 'stated' ('of the doṣas as stated'). 'samyakpītasya' may also be read 'of one who has drunk properly'. raktapitta = haemorrhagic disorder (standard).

hindi: असमय में और अधिक पिया हुआ धूम उपद्रव उत्पन्न करता है। उसमें सर्पि का पान, नावन, अञ्जन और तर्पण इष्ट है,
english: Smoke drunk at the wrong time and in excess would cause complications. In that case drinking of ghee (sarpis), nasal therapy (nāvana), collyrium (añjana) and tarpaṇa are recommended,

text_flags.why: a + iṣṭam gives 'tatreṣṭaṃ'; 'tatraeṣṭaṃ' leaves the vowel sandhi undone and gives 9 syllables in the pāda instead of 8; probable typo.

notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. tarpaṇa: a satiating/nourishing measure; here probably the eye treatment of that name beside añjana, but it may also mean a nourishing drink. 'iṣṭam' is singular for the whole list. The sentence continues into unit 40 ('snaihikam ... yadi').

hindi: धूम से उत्पन्न दोष में, यदि वायु पित्त का अनुगामी हो, तो स्नैहिक; रक्तपित्त में तो शीत, और श्लेष्म-पित्त में विरूक्षण होना चाहिए।
english: in a disorder (doṣa) born of smoke, if Vāta (vāyu) follows Pitta, the unctuous (measure); but in raktapitta the cold should be used, and in Kapha (śleṣman) with Pitta, drying (virūkṣaṇa).

text_flags.why: 'aniga' is not a word; 'anuga' (following) gives the sense 'Vāta following Pitta'; probable typo (i for u).

notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'snaihikam' may describe the measures listed in 39b (nāvana etc. of unctuous kind) rather than a separate measure. 'syāt' is read with all three clauses.
lines_deva: स्नैहिकं धूमजे दोषे वायुः पित्तानिगो यदि
lines_iast: snaihikaṃ dhūmaje doṣe vāyuḥ pittānigo yadi

hindi: अब इसके आगे मैं कहूँगा कि किनके लिए धूम निन्दित है। विरिक्त धूम न पिए, न बस्तिकर्म किए जाने पर,
english: But hereafter I shall declare for whom smoking is condemned. One who has been purged should not drink smoke, nor when an enema procedure (bastikarman) has been done,
lines_deva: परं त्वतः प्रवक्ष्यामि धूमो येषां विगर्हितः
न विरिक्तः पिबेद्धूमं न कृते बस्तिकर्मणि
lines_iast: paraṃ tvataḥ pravakṣyāmi dhūmo yeṣāṃ vigarhitaḥ
na viriktaḥ pibeddhūmaṃ na kṛte bastikarmaṇi

hindi: न रक्तविकारी, न विष से पीड़ित, न शोक करता हुआ, और न गर्भिणी; न श्रम में, न मद में, न आम में, न पित्त में, न प्रजागर में,
english: nor one with a blood disorder (raktin), nor one afflicted by poison, nor one grieving, and not a pregnant woman; not in fatigue, in intoxication, in āma, in Pitta, or in sleeplessness,
notes: raktin: literally 'one having blood', taken as one suffering from a blood disorder such as raktapitta. āma = the undigested state. 'pitte' = in (aggravated) Pitta.
lines_deva: न रक्ती न विषेणार्तो न शोचन्न च गर्भिणी
न श्रमे न मदे नामे न पित्ते न प्रजागरे
lines_iast: na raktī na viṣeṇārto na śocanna ca garbhiṇī
na śrame na made nāme na pitte na prajāgare

hindi: न मूर्च्छा, भ्रम और तृष्णा में, न क्षीण में और न ही क्षत में; न मद्य और दुग्ध पीकर, न स्नेह, और न माक्षिक —
english: not in fainting, giddiness and thirst, not in one wasted, and also not in one injured (kṣata); not after drinking wine and milk, nor sneha (unctuous substance), nor honey (mākṣika),
notes: 'pītvā' (having drunk) is read with madya-dugdhe, sneham and mākṣikam. kṣata often means a chest injury in this text; here only 'injured'. Hindi 'न ही' renders 'nāpi' (not also), not added emphasis.
lines_deva: न मूर्च्छाभ्रमतृष्णासु न क्षीणे नापि च क्षते
न मद्यदुग्धे पीत्वा च न स्नेहं न च माक्षिकम्
lines_iast: na mūrcchābhramatṛṣṇāsu na kṣīṇe nāpi ca kṣate
na madyadugdhe pītvā ca na snehaṃ na ca mākṣikam

hindi: न दधि के साथ भोजन करके धूम, न रूक्ष और न क्रुद्ध; न तालुशोष में, न तिमिर में, और न सिर पर आघात होने पर,
english: nor smoke after eating with curd; not one who is dry, nor one who is angry; not in dryness of the palate, in timira, nor when the head has been struck,

text_flags.why: possible: 'abhihita' (from abhi-√dhā) means 'said, named'; 'struck, injured' requires 'abhihata' (abhi-√han), which the sense needs; the split uses abhihate.

notes: 'eva' is a metrical particle and is not rendered. timira = dimness of vision, sometimes equated with early cataract (probable).
lines_deva: धूमं न भुक्त्वा दध्ना च न रूक्षः क्रुद्ध एव च
न तालुशोषे तिमिरे शिरस्यभिहिते न च
lines_iast: dhūmaṃ na bhuktvā dadhnā ca na rūkṣaḥ kruddha eva ca
na tāluśoṣe timire śirasyabhihite na ca

hindi: न शङ्खक में, न रोहिणी में, न मेह में, न मदात्यय में। इन अकालों में जो मनुष्य मोह से धूम पीता है,
english: not in śaṅkhaka, in rohiṇī, in meha, or in madātyaya. The man who out of delusion drinks smoke at these wrong times —
notes: Disease names kept as Sanskrit. śaṅkhaka = a disease of the temple region (identification disputed); rohiṇī = a throat disease often equated with diphtheria (probable); meha = prameha, urinary disorders including diabetes (standard); madātyaya = disorders from excessive drinking, alcoholism (standard). The sentence continues into unit 46.
lines_deva: न शङ्खके न रोहिण्यां न मेहे न मदात्यये
एषु धूममकालेषु मोहात् पिबति यो नरः
lines_iast: na śaṅkhake na rohiṇyāṃ na mehe na madātyaye
eṣu dhūmamakāleṣu mohāt pibati yo naraḥ

words.gloss: seated in head, nose and eyes

hindi: धूम के विभ्रम से उसके दारुण रोग बढ़ते हैं। जो धूम के योग्य है वह सिर, घ्राण और अक्षि में आश्रित दोष में —
english: his dreadful diseases increase from the misuse of smoke. One fit for smoking should drink, in a doṣa seated in the head, nose and eyes,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins a sentence completed by 'ghrāṇena' at the start of unit 47. vibhrama = error, misuse.

hindi: घ्राण से; कण्ठ में स्थित होने पर मुख से। घ्राण से पीने वाला मुख से निकाले; मुख से धूम के कवल पीता हुआ घ्राण से न निकाले।
english: through the nose; when it is seated in the throat, through the mouth. One who drinks through the nose should emit through the mouth; drinking mouthfuls of smoke through the mouth, one should not emit them through the nose.
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'ghrāṇena' is read with the doṣa of head, nose and eyes in 46b, and 'āsyena' with 'kaṇṭhasthe' (respective order); an alternative reading takes 'ghrāṇena āsyena kaṇṭhasthe' together as 'through nose and mouth when it is in the throat'.

hindi: क्योंकि प्रतिलोम गया हुआ धूम शीघ्र दोनों नेत्रों को हानि पहुँचाएगा। शरीर और नेत्र सीधे रखकर, उसी में चित्त लगाकर, भली-भाँति बैठकर, तीन पर्यायों में —
english: For smoke that goes in the reverse direction would quickly harm the eyes. With body and eyes straight, mind on it, well seated, in three rounds,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the sentence whose verb 'pibet' opens unit 49. The second 'hi' is an expletive particle and is not rendered separately.
lines_deva: प्रतिलोमं गतो ह्याशु धूमो हिंस्याद्धि चक्षुषी
lines_iast: pratilomaṃ gato hyāśu dhūmo hiṃsyāddhi cakṣuṣī

hindi: आत्मवान् एक छिद्र बन्द करके नासिका से धूम पिए। वैरेचन में नेत्र अपनी अंगुलियों से चौबीस का,
english: the self-controlled one should drink the smoke through the nose, closing one opening. In evacuative (virecana) smoking the pipe (netra) is of twenty-four, by one's own fingers,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the pipe measurements continued in unit 50. netra here = the smoking pipe. 'twenty-four' is of finger-breadths (aṅgula), as the next unit shows.

words.gloss: with tip measured as a kola stone

hindi: स्नेह में बत्तीस अंगुल का, प्रयोग में डेढ़ गुना इष्ट है। सीधा, तीन कोषों वाला, अफलित, और कोल की गुठली के माप के अग्र वाला —
english: in the unctuous, of thirty-two finger-breadths; in regular smoking, one and a half (times) is desired. Straight, with three compartments (koṣa) and not split, its tip of the measure of a kola stone,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'adhyardham' is usually taken as one and a half times 24, i.e. 36 finger-breadths for the regular (prāyogika) pipe; the text does not state the base. 'trikoṣāphalitam': read as tri-koṣa + aphalita 'not split/cracked'; the meaning of aphalita here is uncertain. kola = jujube, Ziziphus mauritiana (standard). Review: 'trikoṣāphalitam' can equally be split tri-koṣa + āphalitam (a + ā = ā); neither sense is certain.

words.gloss: of the same material as an enema nozzle

hindi: बस्तिनेत्र के समान द्रव्य वाला धूमनेत्र प्रशस्त है। दूर से निकला हुआ, पर्वों से कटा हुआ, नाड़ी से पतला किया हुआ,
english: A smoking pipe (dhūmanetra) of the same material as an enema nozzle (bastinetra) is commended. Coming out from afar, broken by the joints, thinned by the tube,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 describes the smoke (dhūmaḥ, in unit 52). parvan = the joints (nodes) of the pipe.

hindi: मात्रा और काल से सेवित धूम इन्द्रिय को बाधा नहीं पहुँचाता। और जब उर, कण्ठ और सिर हल्केपन को प्राप्त हों,
english: smoke used in (due) measure and time does not harm the sense faculty (indriya). And when the chest, throat and head attain lightness,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'indriyam' is singular in the text (collective).
lines_deva: यदा चोरश्च कण्ठश्च शिरश्च लघुतां व्रजेत्
lines_iast: yadā coraśca kaṇṭhaśca śiraśca laghutāṃ vrajet

hindi: और कफ पतलेपन को प्राप्त हो, तो धूम को सुपीत बताए। जिसका स्वर अविशुद्ध हो और कण्ठ कफ-युक्त हो,
english: and Kapha has become thin, one should declare the smoke well drunk. One whose voice is unclear, and whose throat is with Kapha,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the signs of insufficient smoking completed in unit 54.
lines_deva: अविशुद्धः स्वरो यस्य कण्ठश्च सकफो भवेत्
lines_iast: aviśuddhaḥ svaro yasya kaṇṭhaśca sakapho bhavet

hindi: और मस्तक स्तिमित हो — इस प्रकार धूम को अपीत बताए। तालु, मूर्धा और कण्ठ सूखते हैं, तपते हैं,
english: and whose head is heavy and numb (stimita) — thus one should declare the smoke not drunk. Palate, head and throat dry up and burn,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the signs of excessive smoking, which run through unit 56a. 'apīta' (not drunk) contrasts with 'supīta' (well drunk) in unit 53, i.e. insufficient smoking. 'śuṣyate' and 'paritapyate' are singular with several subjects.
lines_deva: तालु मूर्धा च कण्ठश्च शुष्यते परितप्यते
lines_iast: tālu mūrdhā ca kaṇṭhaśca śuṣyate paritapyate

hindi: प्राणी तृषित होता है, मोहित होता है, और रक्त अधिक बहता है, सिर अत्यधिक घूमता है, और उसे मूर्च्छा उत्पन्न होती है,
english: the person (jantu) becomes thirsty and confused, blood flows in excess, the head spins exceedingly, and fainting arises in him,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'jantū raktam' is regular sandhi of 'jantuḥ raktam' (visarga dropped before r, vowel lengthened). 'tṛṣyate', 'muhyate', 'sravate' are middle forms of verbs usually active (tṛṣyati, muhyati, sravati); kept as printed.
lines_deva: तृष्यते मुह्यते जन्तू रक्तं च स्रवतेऽधिकम्
lines_iast: tṛṣyate muhyate jantū raktaṃ ca sravate'dhikam

hindi: धूम के अत्यधिक सेवन किए जाने पर इन्द्रियाँ उपतप्त होती हैं। और मनुष्य वर्ष-प्रतिवर्ष तीन कालों में अणुतैल का सेवन करे —
english: the senses are afflicted when smoke is used excessively. And year after year a man should use Aṇu oil (aṇutaila) at three seasons,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 1 ends the section on smoking, line 2 begins the section on nasal oil (nasya), continued in unit 57. 'nā' is the nominative singular of nṛ 'man', not the negative.
lines_deva: वर्षे वर्षेऽणुतैलं च कालेषु त्रिषु ना चरेत्
lines_iast: varṣe varṣe'ṇutailaṃ ca kāleṣu triṣu nā caret

words.gloss: in the rains, autumn and spring

hindi: प्रावृट्, शरद् और वसन्त में, जब आकाश मेघरहित हो। जो यथाकाल यथोक्त नस्यकर्म का सेवन करता है,
english: in the rains (prāvṛṣ), autumn and spring, when the sky is cloudless. Whoever practises nasal therapy (nasya) at the proper time, as prescribed,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37.

hindi: उसका न चक्षु, न घ्राण, न श्रोत्र उपहत होता है; और उसके केश या श्मश्रु न श्वेत होते हैं, न कपिल।
english: neither his eye, nor nose, nor ear is impaired; nor again would his hair or beard become white or tawny.
notes: 'punaḥ' (again) is rendered 'again'.
lines_deva: न तस्य चक्षुर्न घ्राणं न श्रोत्रमुपहन्यते
न स्युः श्वेता न कपिलाः केशाः श्मश्रूणि वा पुनः
lines_iast: na tasya cakṣurna ghrāṇaṃ na śrotramupahanyate
na syuḥ śvetā na kapilāḥ keśāḥ śmaśrūṇi vā punaḥ

hindi: और केश झड़ते नहीं, और विशेष रूप से बढ़ते हैं। मन्यास्तम्भ, शिरःशूल, अर्दित, हनुसंग्रह,
english: and the hairs do not fall out, and they grow especially. Stiffness of the neck (manyāstambha), headache, ardita, seizure of the jaw (hanusaṃgraha),
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the list of diseases whose verb 'śāmyati' is in unit 60. ardita = facial palsy (standard); hanusaṃgraha = lockjaw, trismus (probable); manyāstambha = neck stiffness, torticollis (probable).
lines_deva: न च केशाः प्रमुच्यन्ते वर्धन्ते च विशेषतः
lines_iast: na ca keśāḥ pramucyante vardhante ca viśeṣataḥ

hindi: पीनस और अर्धावभेद, और सिर का कम्पन शान्त होता है। शिर और कपाल की सिराएँ, सन्धियाँ, स्नायु और कण्डराएँ,
english: pīnasa and ardhāvabheda (one-sided headache), and tremor of the head subside. The vessels (sirā), joints, ligaments (snāyu) and tendons (kaṇḍarā) of the head and skull,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'śāmyati' is singular for the whole list of 59b-60a. pīnasa = chronic rhinitis or coryza (standard); ardhāvabheda(ka) = hemicrania, migraine-like headache (probable). 'śiraḥkapālānām' may also be read 'of the skull-bones of the head' (tat-puruṣa).

hindi: — उसके, नावन से तृप्त होकर, अधिक बल प्राप्त करते हैं। मुख प्रसन्न और उपचित, स्वर स्निग्ध, स्थिर और महान्,
english: of his, nourished by nasal therapy (nāvana), gain greater strength. The face is bright and full, the voice smooth, steady and great,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 1 completes the subject list of 60b. 'nāvanaprīṇitāḥ' is feminine plural, agreeing with the nearest nouns (sirāḥ, snāyukaṇḍarāḥ). mukha may also mean 'mouth'.
lines_deva: मुखं प्रसन्नोपचितं स्वरः स्निग्धः स्थिरो महान्
lines_iast: mukhaṃ prasannopacitaṃ svaraḥ snigdhaḥ sthiro mahān

hindi: सब इन्द्रियों की निर्मलता, और बल अधिक होता है; और उसे ऊर्ध्वजत्रुज रोग सहसा नहीं होते।
english: there is clarity of all the senses, and strength becomes greater; and diseases arising above the collar-bones (ūrdhvajatru) do not suddenly arise in him.
notes: 'bhavati' may be read with both 'vaimalyam' and 'balam'.

words.gram: compound member (stem; dvandva dārvītvak-madhukam, n. acc. sg.)
n. acc. sg. (last member of dvandva dārvītvak-madhukam)

hindi: और जीर्ण होते हुए के उत्तमाङ्गों में जरा बल नहीं पाती। चन्दन और अगुरु, पत्र, दार्वीत्वक्, मधुक, बला,
english: And in the head (uttamāṅga) of one growing old, old age does not gain strength. Candana and aguru, patra, bark of dārvī, madhuka, balā,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the list of drugs for Aṇu oil, governed by 'vipācayet' in unit 66. uttamāṅga ('highest limb') = the head; plural here. Identifications: candana = Santalum album (standard); aguru = Aquilaria agallocha (standard); patra = tejapatra, Cinnamomum tamala (probable); dārvī = Berberis aristata, Hindi दारुहल्दी (standard); madhuka = yaṣṭimadhu, Glycyrrhiza glabra, Hindi मुलेठी (standard); balā = Sida cordifolia, Hindi खरेटी (standard).

words.gram: compound member (stem; dvandva tvak-mustam, n. acc. sg.)
n. acc. sg. (last member of dvandva tvak-mustam)

hindi: प्रपौण्डरीक, सूक्ष्मैला, विडङ्ग, बिल्व, उत्पल, ह्रीबेर, अभय, वन्य, त्वक्, मुस्त, सारिवा, स्थिरा,
english: prapauṇḍarīka, small elā, viḍaṅga, bilva, utpala, hrībera, abhaya, vanya, tvak, musta, sārivā, sthirā,
notes: Identifications: prapauṇḍarīka = disputed (a Nelumbo/lotus kind and other plants proposed); sūkṣmailā = small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum, Hindi छोटी इलायची (standard); viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes, Hindi वायविडंग (standard); bilva = Aegle marmelos, Hindi बेल (standard); utpala = a water-lily, Nymphaea species (probable); hrībera = disputed (Pavonia odorata, Plectranthus vettiveroides proposed), Hindi सुगन्धबाला; abhaya (neuter) = uśīra, vetiver, Vetiveria zizanioides, Hindi खस (probable, per commentary; not abhayā = harītakī); vanya = kaivarta-mustaka, a Cyperus species (probable); tvak = cinnamon bark, Cinnamomum zeylanicum, Hindi दालचीनी (standard); musta = Cyperus rotundus, Hindi नागरमोथा (standard); sārivā = Hemidesmus indicus, Hindi अनन्तमूल (standard); sthirā = śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum, Hindi सरिवन (standard).

hindi: जीवन्ती और पृश्निपर्णी, सुरदारु, शतावरी, हरेणु, बृहती, व्याघ्री, सुरभी, पद्मकेशर —
english: jīvantī and pṛśniparṇī, suradāru, śatāvarī, hareṇu, bṛhatī, vyāghrī, surabhī, lotus filaments (padmakeśara) —

text_flags.why: 'vyādhrī' is not a known word; vyāghrī (kaṇṭakārī) is the plant regularly paired with bṛhatī; probable typo (dh for gh).

notes: Identifications: jīvantī = Leptadenia reticulata (probable); pṛśniparṇī = Uraria picta (standard); suradāru = devadāru, Cedrus deodara, Hindi देवदार (standard); śatāvarī = Asparagus racemosus, Hindi शतावर (standard); hareṇu = reṇukā, seeds of Vitex agnus-castus (disputed); bṛhatī = Solanum indicum, Hindi बड़ी कटेरी (standard); vyāghrī = kaṇṭakārī, Solanum virginianum (xanthocarpum), Hindi छोटी कटेरी (standard); surabhī = disputed (rāsnā, śallakī and others proposed); padmakeśara = stamens of Nelumbo nucifera (standard).

hindi: सौ गुने शुद्ध माहेन्द्र जल में पकाए; तेल से दस गुना शेष रहे कषाय को उतार ले।
english: one should boil in a hundredfold of pure māhendra water; one should take down the decoction (kaṣāya) remaining at ten times the oil.
notes: māhendra water = rain-water fallen from the sky (as commonly explained); the text says only 'māhendra'. The object of 'vipācayet' is the drugs listed in units 63-65.

hindi: उस कषाय से तेल को दस बार पकाए। फिर उसके दसवें पाक में समान भाग बकरी का दूध
english: With that decoction one should cook the oil ten times. Then at its tenth cooking, goat's milk in equal portion
notes: The sentence continues into unit 68 ('dadyāt'). 'samāṃśam' may also be adverbial ('in equal proportion').
lines_deva: अथास्य दशमे पाके समांशं छागलं पयः
lines_iast: athāsya daśame pāke samāṃśaṃ chāgalaṃ payaḥ

hindi: डाले। यह नावनीय अणुतैल की विधि है। इस तेल की आधे पल के माप की मात्रा का प्रयोग करे,
english: one should add. This is the preparation of Aṇu oil for nasal use. One should apply a dose of this oil measuring half a pala,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 continues into unit 69 (for whom and how the dose is applied). pala is a weight unit; the text gives no conversion.

words.gloss: of one whose head is oleated and fomented

hindi: जिसका उत्तमाङ्ग स्निग्ध और स्विन्न किया गया हो, उसके लिए पिचु से तीन नावनों द्वारा। तीन-तीन दिन के बाद, सात दिन तक यह कर्म करे,
english: for one whose head (uttamāṅga) has been oleated and fomented, with a swab (picu), in three nasal applications. Every third day, for seven days, one should perform this procedure,

text_flags.why: 'etata' is not a form; 'etat' (this), with 'karma', is needed, and the extra syllable makes the pāda 9 syllables instead of 8; probable typo.

notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'tryahāt tryahāt ca saptāham' is ambiguous: 'every third day for seven days', or (as many take it) seven applications at three-day intervals; the literal rendering is given. 'nāvanaiḥ tribhiḥ' may mean three applications at each sitting.

hindi: निवात और उष्ण का आचरण करने वाला, हिताशी और नियतेन्द्रिय। त्रिदोषनाशक और इन्द्रियों को बल देने वाले इस तेल का —
english: keeping to windless and warm conditions, eating what is wholesome, with senses controlled. This oil, which destroys the three doṣas and gives strength to the senses —
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 1 describes the person in 69b, line 2 is the object of 'prayuñjānaḥ' in unit 71.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. mid. pra-√yuj

hindi: यथाकाल प्रयोग करता हुआ यथोक्त गुणों को प्राप्त करता है। कुचले हुए अग्र वाला, कषाय, कटु और तिक्त, दोनों कालों में
english: applying it at the proper time, one obtains the benefits (guṇa) as stated. With crushed tip, astringent, pungent and bitter, at the two times,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the tooth-stick (dantapavana) passage, whose noun and verb are in unit 72. 'kaṣāya-kaṭu-tiktakam' may mean of any of these tastes.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. caus. √bādh

words.gloss: born of tongue, teeth and mouth

hindi: दन्तपवन को, दन्तमांस को पीड़ा न देते हुए, चबाए। यह गन्ध, विरसता, और जिह्वा, दाँत और मुख से उत्पन्न मल को नष्ट करता है,
english: one should chew the tooth-stick (dantapavana), without hurting the gums. It removes odour, distaste, and the waste (mala) born of the tongue, teeth and mouth,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. The subject of 'nihanti' is 'dantaviśodhanam' in unit 73.

words.gloss: karañja, karavīra, arka, mālatī, kakubha and asana

hindi: दन्तविशोधन उसे निकालकर तुरन्त रुचि उत्पन्न करता है। करञ्ज, करवीर, अर्क, मालती, ककुभ और असन
english: the tooth-cleanser, having drawn it out, at once produces relish. Karañja, karavīra, arka, mālatī, kakubha and asana
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37. 'niṣkṛṣya' (having drawn out) most likely refers to the waste (mala) of unit 72. Identifications: karañja = Pongamia pinnata, Hindi करंज (standard); karavīra = Nerium oleander, Hindi कनेर (standard); arka = Calotropis procera / gigantea, Hindi आक (standard); mālatī = Jasminum grandiflorum, Hindi चमेली (probable; Aganosma also proposed); kakubha = Terminalia arjuna, Hindi अर्जुन (standard); asana = Pterocarpus marsupium, Hindi विजयसार (standard).

hindi: दन्तपवन के लिए प्रशस्त हैं, और जो इसी प्रकार के वृक्ष हैं वे भी। सुवर्ण, रूप्य और ताम्र के, और त्रपु तथा रीति से बने
english: are commended for the tooth-stick, and also trees which are of this kind. Of gold, silver and copper, and made of tin and brass,
notes: GROUPING: see unit 37; line 2 begins the tongue-scraper passage, whose noun 'jihvānirlekhanāni' is in unit 75 (next chunk). trapu = tin (sometimes lead); rīti = brass.

hindi: जिह्वा-निर्लेखन तीक्ष्ण न हों और टेढ़े हों; और जो मल जिह्वा के मूल में स्थित है और उच्छ्वास को रोकता है,
english: Tongue-scrapers should be not sharp and curved; and the waste (mala) which lies at the root of the tongue and obstructs breathing,
notes: The relative clause 'yat ... malam' is completed by 'tena' in 76a; the sentence runs on into 76. anṛju 'not straight' = curved (bent so as to scrape).

hindi: उससे दुर्गन्ध प्राप्त होती है; इसलिए जिह्वा को खुरचना चाहिए। वैशद्य, रुचि और सौगन्ध्य चाहने वाले को मुख से ये धारण करने चाहिए:
english: by that one acquires foul smell; therefore one should scrape the tongue. One who desires clearness (vaiśadya), relish and fragrance should hold with the mouth the following:
notes: 'tena' picks up the relative clause of 75b. 76b introduces the list of mouth-fresheners in 77; the sentence continues into 77 (not a grouping error). Subject of 'bhajate' is unexpressed (one / the person).

hindi: जाती, कटुक और पूग के तथा लवङ्ग के फल; कक्कोल का फल, तथा ताम्बूल का शुभ पत्र; तथा कर्पूर-निर्यास और सूक्ष्म एला के फल।
english: the fruits of jātī, kaṭuka and pūga, and of lavaṅga; the fruit of kakkola, and likewise the fine leaf of tāmbūla; likewise the exudate of karpūra, and the fruits of the small elā.
notes: Identifications (notes only): jātī(phala) = nutmeg, Myristica fragrans (standard); pūga = areca nut, Areca catechu (standard); lavaṅga = clove, Syzygium aromaticum (standard; the 'fruits' are the dried buds); kakkola = cubeb, Piper cubeba (probable; disputed); tāmbūla = betel leaf, Piper betle (standard); karpūra = camphor, from Cinnamomum camphora (standard); sūkṣmailā = small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum (standard). kaṭuka: disputed; it may be a separate item, or 'jātī-kaṭuka' may be read together as one item (the pungent jātī fruit, i.e. nutmeg); taken here as a three-member dvandva. Three printed lines in one numbered verse, as in the edition.
lines_deva: कक्कोलस्य फलं पत्रं ताम्बूलस्य शुभं तथा
lines_iast: kakkolasya phalaṃ patraṃ tāmbūlasya śubhaṃ tathā

hindi: हनुओं का बल, स्वर का बल, मुख का उत्तम उपचय, और उत्तम रस-ज्ञान, और अन्न में श्रेष्ठ रुचि होती है।
english: There would be strength of the jaws, strength of voice, excellent fullness of the face, excellent perception of taste (rasa), and the best relish for food.
notes: These results (78–80) belong to holding oil in the mouth (taila-gaṇḍūṣa-dhāraṇa), named only in 80b; 78–80 are one statement. Optative 'syāt' rendered 'there would be'.
lines_deva: स्यात् परं च रसज्ञानमन्ने च रुचिरुत्तमा
lines_iast: syāt paraṃ ca rasajñānamanne ca ruciruttamā

hindi: और उसे कण्ठ-शोष नहीं होता, न ओठों के फटने का भय रहता है; और दाँत क्षय को प्राप्त नहीं होते और दृढ़-मूल होते हैं।
english: And he would have no dryness of the throat, nor fear of cracking of the lips; and the teeth do not decay, and they become firm-rooted.
notes: Continues the results of oil-holding (see 80b).
lines_deva: न च दन्ताः क्षयं यान्ति दृढमूला भवन्ति च
lines_iast: na ca dantāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti dṛḍhamūlā bhavanti ca

words.gloss: from holding a mouthful of oil

hindi: तैल-गण्डूष-धारण से दाँतों में शूल नहीं होता, न अम्ल से उनमें सिहरन होती है, और वे अत्यन्त कठोर भक्ष्यों को भी चबा लेते हैं।
english: From holding a mouthful of oil (taila-gaṇḍūṣa), the teeth do not ache, nor are they set on edge by sour things, and they chew even very hard foods.
notes: Subject 'teeth' is carried over from 79b. hṛṣyante: 'dantaharṣa', the teeth being set on edge (hypersensitivity); Hindi renders it as सिहरन (tingling). 'parān' taken adverbially-adjectivally as 'extremely (hard)'; alternatively 'other (hard) foods'.
lines_deva: न शूल्यन्ते न चाम्लेन हृष्यन्ते भक्षयन्ति च
lines_iast: na śūlyante na cāmlena hṛṣyante bhakṣayanti ca

words.gloss: whose head is moist with sneha

hindi: जिसका सिर नित्य स्नेह से आर्द्र रहता है उसे शिरःशूल नहीं होता; न खालित्य, न पालित्य, और न केश झड़ते हैं।
english: For one whose head is always moist with oil (sneha), headache does not arise; there is no baldness, no greying, nor do the hairs fall out.
notes: khālitya and pālitya are the Āyurvedic names for baldness/alopecia and premature greying (standard).
lines_deva: न खालित्यं न पालित्यं न केशाः प्रपतन्ति च
lines_iast: na khālityaṃ na pālityaṃ na keśāḥ prapatanti ca

hindi: शिर के कपालों का बल विशेष रूप से बढ़ता है; और केश दृढ़-मूल, लम्बे और काले होते हैं।
english: The strength of the skull-bones increases especially, and the hairs become firm-rooted, long and black.
lines_deva: दृढमूलाश्च दीर्घाश्च कृष्णाः केशा भवन्ति च
lines_iast: dṛḍhamūlāśca dīrghāśca kṛṣṇāḥ keśā bhavanti ca

hindi: सिर पर तैल-निषेवण से इन्द्रियाँ प्रसन्न होती हैं, मुख अच्छी त्वचा वाला होता है, और निद्रा-लाभ तथा सुख होता है।
english: From the use of oil on the head the senses become clear, the face has good skin, and there would be getting of sleep and happiness.
notes: 'sukham' may be a second subject ('and happiness') or adverbial ('getting sleep easily'); the first is followed in the translation. 'mūrdhni' (loc.) goes with 'taila-niṣevaṇāt': use of oil on the head.

hindi: नित्य कर्ण-तर्पण से वात से उत्पन्न कर्ण-रोग नहीं होते, न मन्या और हनु का संग्रह होता है, न ऊँचा सुनना, न बाधिर्य होता है।
english: From daily karṇatarpaṇa (filling the ears with oil) there are no ear diseases arising from Vāta, no stiffness of the neck (manyā) and jaw, no hearing only of loud sounds, and no deafness.

text_flags.why: the word for deafness is bādhirya (from badhira); v for b is a common confusion

notes: 'uccaiḥ śrutiḥ' = hearing only when spoken loudly, i.e. hardness of hearing. manyā = the side/back muscles of the neck; manyā-hanu-saṃgraha is stiffness of neck and jaw (torticollis / lockjaw-like states; probable). karṇatarpaṇa = ear-oiling ('satiating the ears').

hindi: जैसे स्नेह-अभ्यङ्ग से घड़ा, स्नेह-विमर्दन से चर्म, और उपाङ्ग से अक्ष दृढ़ और क्लेश सहने योग्य हो जाता है,
english: Just as a pot from being smeared with oil, leather from being rubbed with oil, and an axle from lubrication become firm and able to bear strain,
notes: The simile is completed by 'tathā' in 86a; 85–86 are one sentence. upāṅga = greasing (of an axle).

hindi: वैसे ही अभ्यङ्ग से शरीर दृढ़ और अच्छी त्वचा वाला हो जाता है, उसकी मारुत-जनित बाधा शान्त हो जाती है, और वह क्लेश तथा व्यायाम को सहने योग्य होता है।
english: so from massage (abhyaṅga) the body becomes firm and of good skin, with its troubles from Vāta (māruta) calmed, and able to endure strain and exercise.

hindi: स्पर्शन में वायु अधिक होता है, और स्पर्शन त्वचा पर आश्रित है; और अभ्यङ्ग त्वचा के लिए परम हितकर है; इसलिए मनुष्य को उसका नियमित सेवन करना चाहिए।
english: Vāta (vāyu) predominates in the sense of touch (sparśana), and the sense of touch resides in the skin; and massage is supremely beneficial to the skin; therefore a man should practise it regularly.
notes: 'param' may also be read as an adjective with abhyaṅgaḥ ('the best thing for the skin'); sense is the same.

hindi: और अभ्यङ्ग-सेवी का शरीर अभिघात से आहत होने पर, अथवा कभी बल-कर्म में, अत्यधिक विकार को प्राप्त नहीं होता।
english: And the body of one who practises massage, when struck by an injury, or at any time in strenuous work, does not undergo excessive disorder.

words.gloss: with limbs smooth to touch and well-built

hindi: नित्य अभ्यङ्ग से मनुष्य सुस्पर्श और उपचित अङ्गों वाला, बलवान्, प्रियदर्शन और अल्प-जरा वाला भी होता है।
english: From regular massage a man becomes one whose limbs are smooth to the touch and well-built, strong, pleasing to look at, and also of little ageing.

text_flags.why: metre: 'bhavatyaṅganityatvān' has 7 syllables where 8 are needed; 'abhyaṅga' (the topic of 85–89) restores both metre and sense; the printed 'aṅga' looks like a lost 'bhya'

notes: Split follows the suggested reading abhyaṅga-nityatvāt; the printed token gives aṅga-nityatvāt 'from constancy of the limbs', which makes poor sense.

hindi: पाद-अभ्यङ्ग के निषेवण से पैरों का खरत्व, स्तब्धता, रूक्षता, श्रम और सुप्ति तत्काल शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: Roughness, stiffness, dryness, fatigue and numbness of the feet subside immediately from the practice of foot-massage.

text_flags.why: 'viṣevaṇa' is not a word; 'niṣevaṇa' (use, practice) is the form used elsewhere in this chapter (83b, 96b); typing error v for n

notes: 'sadya eva' rendered 'immediately'. supti = numbness (loss of sensation).
lines_deva: खरत्वं स्तब्धता रौक्ष्यं श्रमः सुप्तिश्च पादयोः
lines_iast: kharatvaṃ stabdhatā raukṣyaṃ śramaḥ suptiśca pādayoḥ

hindi: और पैरों में सौकुमार्य, बल और स्थिरता उत्पन्न होती है; दृष्टि प्रसाद को प्राप्त होती है और मारुत शान्त होता है।
english: And softness, strength and steadiness of the feet arise; the sight gains clarity, and Vāta (māruta) is calmed.
lines_deva: जायते सौकुमार्यं च बलं स्थैर्यं च पादयोः
lines_iast: jāyate saukumāryaṃ ca balaṃ sthairyaṃ ca pādayoḥ

hindi: पाद-अभ्यङ्ग से न गृध्रसी-वात होता है, न पैरों का स्फुटन, और न पैरों में सिरा और स्नायु का संकोच होता है।
english: By foot-massage there would be no gṛdhrasī-vāta, no cracking of the feet, and no contraction of the vessels (sirā) and sinews (snāyu) in the feet.
notes: gṛdhrasī = sciatica (standard). The second 'pādayoḥ' is read as locative ('in the feet'); the first as genitive.
lines_deva: न च स्याद्गृध्रसीवातः पादयोः स्फुटनं न च
lines_iast: na ca syādgṛdhrasīvātaḥ pādayoḥ sphuṭanaṃ na ca

hindi: शरीर-परिमार्जन दुर्गन्ध, गौरव, तन्द्रा, कण्डू, मल, अरोचक और स्वेद की बीभत्सता को नष्ट करता है।
english: Rubbing the body (parimārjana) removes foul smell, heaviness, drowsiness, itching, dirt (mala), loss of relish (arocaka) and the loathsomeness of sweat.
notes: parimārjana is usually understood as rubbing/cleansing the body (by commentators as udvartana, rubbing with powders); the text says only 'rubbing'. arocaka = anorexia (standard).

hindi: स्नान पवित्र, वृष्य, आयुष्य, श्रम-स्वेद-मल को दूर करने वाला, शरीर के बल का संधान करने वाला और परम ओजस्कर है।
english: Bathing is purifying, aphrodisiac (vṛṣya), promotes life, removes fatigue, sweat and dirt, restores bodily strength, and is supremely productive of ojas (vital essence).
notes: sandhāna literally 'joining, uniting'; here 'restoring/sustaining' bodily strength.

hindi: निर्मल वस्त्र का धारण काम्य, यशस्य, आयुष्य, अलक्ष्मी-नाशक, प्रहर्षक, श्रीमत्, पारिषद और प्रशस्त है।
english: Wearing clean clothes is pleasing, brings fame, promotes life, destroys misfortune (alakṣmī), gladdens, is graceful, fit for assemblies, and commended.

hindi: गन्ध और माल्य का निषेवण वृष्य, सौगन्ध्य, आयुष्य, काम्य, पुष्टि और बल देने वाला, सौमनस्य और अलक्ष्मी-नाशक है।
english: The use of perfumes and garlands is aphrodisiac, yields fragrance, promotes life, is pleasing, gives nourishment and strength, yields cheerfulness, and destroys misfortune (alakṣmī).

text_flags.why: metre (9 syllables in the first half of the line) and the parallels in 94–99 give āyuṣyam; 'āyuṣayaṃ' is a typing error
'-ghna' (destroying) as in 95a; 'ghra' is a typing error

notes: saugandhya and saumanasya are abstract nouns used as predicates ('is fragrance', 'is cheerfulness', i.e. brings them); kept literal in translation.

hindi: रत्न और आभरण का धारण धन्य, मङ्गल्य, आयुष्य, श्रीमत्, व्यसन-नाशक, हर्षक, काम्य और ओजस्य है।
english: Wearing gems and ornaments brings fortune, is auspicious, promotes life, is graceful, removes calamity (vyasana), gladdens, is pleasing, and promotes ojas.
notes: ratnābharaṇa may also be 'ornaments of gems' (tat-puruṣa) rather than 'gems and ornaments' (dvandva).

hindi: पैरों और मल-मार्गों का बार-बार शौच करना मेध्य, पवित्र, आयुष्य और अलक्ष्मी तथा कलि का नाशक है।
english: Frequent cleansing of the feet and the excretory passages (mala-mārga) promotes intellect (medhya), is purifying, promotes life, and destroys misfortune (alakṣmī) and strife (kali).
notes: kali = strife, discord (or ill luck).

hindi: केश, श्मश्रु, नख आदि का कल्पन और संप्रसाधन पौष्टिक, वृष्य, आयुष्य, शुचि और रूप को निखारने वाला है।
english: Trimming and dressing of hair, beard, nails and the like is nourishing, aphrodisiac, promotes life, is clean, and brightens the appearance.

hindi: पादत्र का धारण चक्षुष्य, स्पर्शन के लिए हितकर, पैरों के व्यसन को दूर करने वाला, बल्य, पराक्रम को सुखद बनाने वाला और वृष्य है।
english: Wearing footwear (pādatra) is good for the eyes, beneficial to the sense of touch (sparśana), removes injury (vyasana) to the feet, is strengthening, makes exertion easy, and is aphrodisiac.

text_flags.why: metathesis: 'spraśana' for 'sparśana' (touch), the word used in 87a

notes: parākrama here probably 'exertion, moving about (walking)'.

words.gloss: keeping off heat, wind, dust and rain

hindi: छत्र-धारण ईति का प्रशमन करने वाला, बल्य, गुप्ति, आवरण और कल्याण करने वाला, तथा घाम, वायु, रज और जल को रोकने वाला कहा जाता है।
english: Carrying an umbrella is said to ward off calamity (īti), to be strengthening, to give protection, cover and welfare, and to keep off heat, wind, dust and rain.
notes: īti = calamity (in the classical lists, plagues such as excessive rain, drought, locusts). 'śaṅkara' = conferring welfare; it may also be read 'guptyāvaraṇa-śaṅkaram' = giving the welfare of protective cover. 'rajombu' = rajaḥ + ambu; no avagraha inside the compound, as usual in print.

hindi: दण्ड-धारण लड़खड़ाने वाले को सहारा देने वाला, और शत्रुओं का नाशक, अवलम्बन, आयुष्य और भय को दूर करने वाला है।
english: Carrying a staff is a support for one who stumbles, a destroyer of enemies, a prop, promotes life, and removes fear.

hindi: जैसे नगर का स्वामी नगर के प्रति और रथी रथ के प्रति, वैसे ही बुद्धिमान् को अपने शरीर के कृत्यों में सावधान रहना चाहिए।
english: As a city-lord for his city, and as a chariot-owner for his chariot, so the wise man should be attentive in the duties of his own body.
notes: nagarin = owner/lord of a city; rathin = owner or rider of a chariot (also 'chariot-warrior'). 'kṛtyeṣu avahitaḥ' is understood with each comparison.

hindi: और यहाँ यह है — जीविका के जो उपाय धर्म के अविरोधी हों उनका सेवन करना चाहिए, और शम तथा अध्ययन का भी; इस प्रकार वह सुख प्राप्त करता है।
english: And here there is: one should resort to those means of livelihood which are not opposed to dharma, and also to tranquillity and study; thus one attains happiness.
notes: 'bhavati cātra' is the lead-in formula introducing a verse, printed inside line a; it is outside the metre. 'śamam adhyayanaṃ ca' are further objects of 'niṣeveta'.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक — मात्रा, द्रव्य, मात्रा पर आश्रित गुरुता और लघुता; जिन द्रव्यों का अभ्यास निन्दित है, और जिनका प्रशस्त है;
english: Here, the verses: measure (mātrā); substances; heaviness and lightness depending on measure; the substances whose habitual use is censured, and those whose is praised;

text_flags.why: possible: the half-line after the lead-in has 15 syllables, one short of 16; a 'ca' after 'mātrāṃ' would complete the metre. Not applied

notes: 'tatra ślokāḥ' introduces the chapter's summary verses (105–111), one running list of the topics; its predicate 'guṇāḥ ... uktāḥ' comes in 111. The lead-in is outside the metre.
lines_deva: तत्र श्लोकाः --- मात्रा द्रव्याणि मात्रां संश्रित्य गुरुलाघवम्
द्रव्याणां गर्हितोऽभ्यासो येषां, येषां च शस्यते
lines_iast: tatra ślokāḥ --- mātrā dravyāṇi mātrāṃ saṃśritya gurulāghavam
dravyāṇāṃ garhito'bhyāso yeṣāṃ, yeṣāṃ ca śasyate

hindi: अञ्जन; धूमवर्ति; वर्ति की त्रिविध कल्पना; धूमपान के गुण, उसके काल, और पान का मान, और किसके लिए कौन-सा;
english: collyrium (añjana); the smoking-stick (dhūmavarti); the threefold preparation of sticks; the benefits of smoking; its times; and the measure of smoking, and for whom which;
notes: Part of the summary list. 'yasya yat' = which (kind or measure) for whom. 'pāna' here = drinking (inhaling) smoke.
lines_deva: धूमपानगुणाः कालाः पानमानं च यस्य यत्
lines_iast: dhūmapānaguṇāḥ kālāḥ pānamānaṃ ca yasya yat

hindi: व्यापत्ति के चिह्न, भैषज्य; जिनके लिए धूम निषिद्ध है; वह कैसे पीना चाहिए; नेत्र किससे बना हो, और जिसके लिए किस प्रकार का हो;
english: the signs of complications (vyāpatti) and the remedy; for whom smoke is forbidden; how it is to be drunk; of what the tube (netra) is made, and for whom of what kind;
notes: Part of the summary list. netra = the smoking-pipe. 'bhaiṣajyam' = the remedy (for those complications).
lines_deva: पेयो यथा यन्मयं च नेत्रं यस्य च यद्विधम्
lines_iast: peyo yathā yanmayaṃ ca netraṃ yasya ca yadvidham

words.gloss: to be done through the nose

hindi: नस्य-कर्म के गुण; नासिका से जो कार्य है, वह कैसे और कब; दन्तपवन को कैसे चबाना चाहिए, कौन सा, किन गुणों वाला, और क्या;
english: the benefits of nasal therapy (nasya); what is to be done through the nose, how and when; how one should chew the tooth-stick (dantapavana), which one, of what qualities, and what;

text_flags.why: possible: 'yad yadguṇaṃ' (which, of what quality) makes sense; 'yaṅguṇa' is not a word and looks like ṅg typed for dg

notes: Part of the summary list. The final 'ca yat' repeats the relative and adds little; the series of relatives (yat, yathā, yadā) stands for the topics of the chapter.

hindi: किस प्रयोजन से और कौन सी वस्तुएँ कवल-ग्रह में मुख से धारण करनी चाहिए; तैल के जो गुण बताए गए, और शिरस्-तैल के जो गुण हैं;
english: for what purpose and which things are to be held with the mouth in gargling (kavala-graha); the benefits of oil that were indicated, and those which are the benefits of head-oil;
notes: Part of the summary list. 'kavalagrahe' (loc.) is taken with 'dhāryāṇi' (to be held in gargling). kavala = a mouthful moved about in the mouth, as against gaṇḍūṣa (held).
lines_deva: तैलस्य ये गुणा दिष्टाः शिरस्तैलगुणाश्च ये
lines_iast: tailasya ye guṇā diṣṭāḥ śirastailaguṇāśca ye

hindi: कर्ण-तैल में, तथा अभ्यङ्ग में, पाद-अभ्यङ्ग में, अङ्ग-मार्जन में; स्नान में, और शुद्ध वस्त्र में, सौगन्ध्य में, रत्न-धारण में;
english: in ear-oil, likewise in massage, in foot-massage, in rubbing the body; in bathing, and in clean clothing, in fragrance, in wearing gems;
notes: The locatives of 110–111 depend on 'guṇāḥ ... uktāḥ' in 111 (the benefits stated in these matters).
lines_deva: स्नाने वाससि शुद्धे च सौगन्ध्ये रत्नधारणे
lines_iast: snāne vāsasi śuddhe ca saugandhye ratnadhāraṇe

hindi: शौच में, लोमों के संहरण में, पादत्र और छत्र के धारण में, तथा दण्ड-धारण में — इस मात्राशितीय में गुण कहे गए हैं।
english: in cleansing, in removing hair, in wearing footwear and umbrella, and likewise in carrying a staff: the benefits have been stated in this Mātrāśitīya.
notes: End of the summary list (105–111). Mātrāśitīya is the chapter's name ('on the measure of eating'); the word 'chapter' is not in the text. 'tathā' is placed with 'daṇḍadhāraṇe' in the translation; it may also simply mean 'thus (stated)'.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में मात्राशितीय नामक पाँचवाँ अध्याय, पूर्ण।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Ślokasthāna (section), the fifth chapter named Mātrāśitīya, completed.
notes: Colophon. 'samāptaḥ' is printed and is rendered as the participle 'completed' (Hindi पूर्ण), keeping the colophon verbless. Ślokasthāna is the name this edition uses for the first section (also called Sūtrasthāna).
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने मात्राशितीयो नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne mātrāśitīyo nāma pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ
